Hi Lena —

Thanks again for agreeing to start the activation process. Before we provision PO visibility and routing on our side I wanted to collect a quick preference so we can set up your ingest method with minimum friction. Two short options we support today: 

1) Portal onboarding (recommended for >25 invoices/month): secure web portal, SSO, line-level mapping in the UI, automatic PO-match on upload.
2) SMTP/email handshake (good for low-volume initial pilots): send to accounts-payable@redwood-invoices.com with a subject token (we use a 6-char token to route and idempotency).

Quick asks:
- Which method do you prefer for the pilot month?
- Do you need multi-PO-per-file support (one invoice covering multiple PO numbers)?
- Do you require line-level tax breakdowns or a single tax total per invoice?

I attached a draft vendor onboarding form (vendor_onboarding_form_v2.pdf) and a tiny canonical CSV sample (canonical_csv_sample.csv) showing the minimal column set we currently ingest. If SMTP is easier for you we’ll share the subject token and a short checklist for formatting. If you have an SFTP preference, let us know but note that our portal is easiest for a long-term handoff.

Proposed next step: 15-minute call Wed 12/2 to confirm choice and walk through the CSV sample. Are you available 9–11am PT?

Thanks —

Hi Jordan —

Appreciate the clear options. A few answers/clarifications from our side: 
- For the pilot month we prefer SMTP/email handshake so our AP team can continue with current inbox routing and we can test idempotency.
- We do occasionally issue single invoices that reference multiple POs (common for consolidated shipment billing). So we do need multi-PO-per-invoice support or a clear rule for splitting.
- We prefer line-level tax (breakdowns) where possible — gives our GL team better tagging, though we can send a single tax total if the portal requires it.

Couple of follow-ups: 
- Does Redwood require the PO numbers in the subject line for the SMTP flow, or is including them in a CSV/attachment sufficient?
- Is there an allowed max filename length/encoding we should be aware of for PDFs? We sometimes have long descriptive names.

I attached one of our sample invoices so you can confirm layout (supplier_invoice_4478.pdf). We can do the call Wed 12/2 at 10am PT.

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the quick response and the sample invoice — looks good. A few clarifications to help with the SMTP pilot: 

- Subject token: for SMTP we ask suppliers to include our routing token in the email subject (format: [RDW:ABC123]) so our ingest pipeline can route to the right ledger and idempotency mechanism. If you prefer, PO numbers can be in the CSV/attached invoice, but the token in the subject speeds routing and reduces false positives.

- Multi-PO handling: we support two approaches:
  * Single-file, multiple PO column: a CSV row can include PO1|PO2|PO3 in a single field (pipe-delimited) and our parser will expand into match attempts.
  * Split on ingest: if you prefer to send one PDF covering multiple POs, we can accept it but suggest appending a manifest CSV with mapping rows to ensure correct GL attribution.

- Filename limits: keep filenames under 250 bytes and avoid non-UTF8 characters; spaces are fine but prefer underscores for parity. PDFs are accepted up to 10MB.

Attached is canonical_csv_sample.csv showing the minimal columns we require: invoice_number, invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD), supplier_name, total_amount, currency, po_list, tax_total, tax_details (optional JSON string), line_items_link (optional). We included a one-line example.

For the pilot I recommend: SMTP with subject token + manifest CSV for multi-PO invoices, line-level tax in tax_details where available. After 30 days, if volume looks steady we’ll open portal onboarding and migrate you which gives better visibility for POs and remittance.

See you 12/2 at 10am PT — can you confirm the account email you’ll send to (accounts-payable@stellamar.com or a different team alias)?

Best,
Vanessa
Vendor Enablement | Redwood Inference

- Line-level taxes: include tax_details as a JSON string in the tax_details column when possible; otherwise include tax_total as a numeric.
- Filenames: <= 250 bytes, UTF-8. PDFs <= 10MB.
